findings.title: Dict model spec mixing legacy 'params' with 'args'/'kwargs' silently drops params — hyp.reduce returns UNREDUCED data with no warning
findings.description: unpack_model's legacy-dict detection (hypertools/core/shared.py:121) only translates {'model','params'} when NEITHER 'args' NOR 'kwargs' is present. A spec like {'model': 'PCA', 'params': {'n_components': 2}, 'kwargs': {}} — the natural result of a user half-migrating an old script or merging dicts — is treated as canonical: 'params' is copied through as an inert key (shared.py:133 'resolved = dict(m)') and never applied. No DeprecationWarning, no error. Real effect: hyp.reduce(40x10 data) returns 40x10 (PCA fit with default n_components, i.e. no reduction) instead of 40x2. Every downstream consumer of unpack_model (reduce/cluster/align/apply_model/Pipeline) inherits the silent drop. The pure-legacy form {'model','params'} works correctly (returns 40x2 + DeprecationWarning), which makes the mixed form's silent failure especially surprising.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
data = np.random.default_rng(1).normal(size=(40, 10))
r1 = hyp.reduce(data, reduce={'model': 'PCA', 'params': {'n_components': 2}})
print(np.asarray(r1).shape)  # (40, 2) + DeprecationWarning — correct
r2 = hyp.reduce(data, reduce={'model': 'PCA', 'params': {'n_components': 2}, 'kwargs': {}})
print(np.asarray(r2).shape)  # (40, 10) — params silently ignored, no warning
findings.expected: (40, 2) for both, or a loud error/warning that 'params' cannot be combined with 'args'/'kwargs'
findings.actual:
legacy params only -> shape: (40, 2)
params+kwargs mixed -> shape: (40, 10) (if not (40,2), params silently ignored)
[unpack_model output: {'model': <class 'sklearn.decomposition._pca.PCA'>, 'params': {'n_components': 2}, 'kwargs': {}, 'args': []} warnings: []]

findings.title: core/config.ini is dead configuration: zero consumers, and every [plot] value plus [cluster] verbose and [align] algorithm diverge from real runtime defaults
findings.description: configurator.py's module docstring calls itself 'Central default options for hypertools' and a 'single source of truth', but no hypertools code path ever calls get_default_options()/apply_defaults() (grep: the only reference outside core/configurator.py and core/__init__.py is plot/backend.py:918 'bound_args.apply_defaults()', which is inspect.BoundArguments.apply_defaults, unrelated). Editing core/config.ini therefore has NO runtime effect — verified for real: config claims [plot] style='.', linewidth=1, markersize=4, opacity=0.7, cmap=mako, but a default hyp.plot() line artist has linestyle='-', linewidth=1.5, marker=None, markersize=6.0, alpha=None; config claims [reduce] ndims=3, but hyp.reduce(50x10) returns (50,10); [cluster] verbose has no matching cluster() parameter; [align] algorithm='hyper' vs actual signature default model='HyperAlign'. Real defaults are hard-coded in function signatures. A contributor or power user editing config.ini (as the docstring invites) would be silently ignored.

findings.title: Exceptions have no stable documented public import path; internal docstrings disagree (_shared vs core) and hyp.load never documents HypertoolsIOError
findings.description: HypertoolsError/HypertoolsBackendError/HypertoolsIOError are not importable from the hypertools top level (hypertools.HypertoolsError etc. are all AttributeError) and appear nowhere in docs/api.rst or any tutorial. The only import paths are hypertools.core.exceptions (undocumented) and hypertools._shared.exceptions (underscore-private shim). Internal docstrings disagree about the canonical path: io/lsl.py:72 says 'hypertools.core.exceptions.HypertoolsIOError' while io/sources.py:254,388 say ':class:`~hypertools._shared.exceptions.HypertoolsIOError`' (a private path rendered into user-facing API docs). hyp.load's own docstring has no Raises section at all, so a scientist has no documented way to discover what to catch. (Catching OSError does work for IO errors thanks to the mixin — verified — but that is undocumented too.)
findings.repro:
import hypertools
print(hasattr(hypertools, 'HypertoolsError'), hasattr(hypertools, 'exceptions'))
import inspect; print('Raises' in (inspect.getdoc(hypertools.load) or ''))
# grep -n 'exceptions' docs/api.rst  -> no exception classes documented
findings.expected: One documented public path (e.g. hypertools.exceptions or top-level re-export), consistent references in all docstrings, and a Raises section in hyp.load
findings.actual:
hypertools.HypertoolsError: False
hypertools.HypertoolsBackendError: False
hypertools.HypertoolsIOError: False
hypertools.exceptions: False
hyp.load docstring mentions 'HypertoolsIOError': False
lsl_stream docstring mentions 'core.exceptions': True; io/sources.py:254 references hypertools._shared.exceptions.HypertoolsIOError

findings.title: RobustDict returns one shared mutable default object for every missing key (cross-key aliasing), and .get() bypasses the default
findings.description: RobustDict.__getitem__/__missing__ return self.default_value itself, not a copy (hypertools/core/shared.py:63-70). With the configurator's __default_value__={} this means every missing-section lookup aliases ONE dict: mutating the result of opts['typo_a'] makes the mutation appear under every other missing key. Also inconsistent lookup semantics: rd['missing'] returns {} while rd.get('missing') returns None and 'missing' in rd is False, so code switching between [] and .get() sees different values. Low blast radius today (apply_defaults copies immediately), but RobustDict is exported from hypertools.core as public API.
findings.repro:
from hypertools.core.configurator import get_default_options
o = get_default_options()
a = o['missing_a']; a['injected'] = 123
print(o['missing_b'])            # {'injected': 123}
print(o['missing_a'] is o['missing_b'])  # True
from hypertools.core.shared import RobustDict
rd = RobustDict({'x': 1}, __default_value__={})
print(rd['missing'], rd.get('missing'))  # {} None
findings.expected: each missing lookup returns a fresh copy of the default (defaultdict-style factory), and .get() consistent with []
findings.actual:
o2['missing_b'] -> {'injected': 123} (expected {} if safe; {'injected':123} = aliasing)
o2['missing_a'] is o2['missing_b']: True
rd['missing'] -> {} | rd.get('missing') -> None

findings.title: get_default_options/apply_defaults return raw strings for every config value ('3', 'False', '0.7') — 'False' is truthy
findings.description: The dw ConfigParser backend performs no type coercion, so the exported hypertools.core.apply_defaults('cluster') returns {'n_clusters': '3', 'verbose': 'False'} — bool('False') is True and '3' is not an int. Any consumer following the docstring contract ('Return the config defaults for func_name overridden by kwargs') would pass stringly-typed values into sklearn constructors (e.g. KMeans(n_clusters='3') raises; verbose='False' enables verbose). Harmless only because nothing currently consumes it (see -002), but it is exported public API on hypertools.core.

d = apply_defaults('cluster')
print(d, {k: type(v).__name__ for k, v in d.items()})
print(bool(d['verbose']))  # True — despite 'False' in config.ini

None: {'n_clusters': '3', 'verbose': 'False'}

findings.title: Exception constructor signatures inconsistent: subclasses require exactly one 'message' arg and define .message; base HypertoolsError accepts any args and has no .message
findings.description: HypertoolsBackendError() with no args raises TypeError (missing 1 required positional argument: 'message'), and two args also TypeError, while HypertoolsError() and HypertoolsError('a','b') both work; only the subclasses carry a .message attribute. Anyone raising/handling the family generically (or subclassing) hits the asymmetry. The explicit __init__ overrides add nothing beyond .message (pickle works either way — verified).
findings.repro:
from hypertools.core.exceptions import HypertoolsError, HypertoolsBackendError
HypertoolsError()          # ok
HypertoolsBackendError()   # TypeError: missing 1 required positional argument: 'message'
HypertoolsError('a','b')   # ok
HypertoolsBackendError('a','b')  # TypeError
findings.expected: uniform constructor contract across the hierarchy (drop the overrides or add them to the base)
findings.actual:
HypertoolsError() ok (0 args)
HypertoolsBackendError() TypeError: HypertoolsBackendError.__init__() missing 1 required positional argument: 'message'
HypertoolsBackendError 2-arg TypeError: HypertoolsBackendError.__init__() takes 2 positional arguments but 3 were given

findings.title: set_interactive_backend accepts a nonexistent backend name silently; failure surfaces only at the next interactive plot (and module-global switch_backend crashes AttributeError on raw strings)
findings.description: hyp.set_interactive_backend('definitely_not_a_backend') returns without any validation (documented as deferred, but nothing checks the name against matplotlib's known backends), so the user's typo is reported much later — hyp.plot(x, interactive=True) then raises HypertoolsBackendError (good message, chained ModuleNotFoundError). Additionally the module-global hypertools.plot.backend.switch_backend, whose docstring promises 'Raises HypertoolsBackendError if switching the backend fails', crashes with AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'as_python' when handed a plain string (it requires the internal HypertoolsBackend wrapper) — an internal function, but its docstring contract does not hold for the obvious input.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
hyp.set_interactive_backend('definitely_not_a_backend')  # no error
hyp.plot(np.random.default_rng(0).normal(size=(20,4)), interactive=True)  # HypertoolsBackendError here
# internal: from hypertools.plot.backend import switch_backend; switch_backend('nope')  # AttributeError
findings.expected: early validation (raise/warn at set time for unknown backend names); switch_backend either coerces str or documents the HypertoolsBackend requirement
findings.actual:
set_interactive_backend accepted bogus name silently
plot raised: HypertoolsBackendError Failed to switch the plotting backend to definitely_not_a_backend. You may be missing required dependencies, or this backend may not be available for your system
AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'as_python' (backend.py:713, in _switch_backend_regular)

findings.title: shared.get() returns the WHOLE list for out-of-range and negative indices instead of raising or clamping
findings.description: hypertools/core/shared.py get(value, i) returns value[i] only when 0 <= i < len(value); get([1,2,3], 5) and get([1,2,3], -1) both return [1, 2, 3]. For its intended use (per-dataset parameter lists) an out-of-range dataset index silently hands the manipulator the entire list as the parameter value rather than failing loudly — a shape/typo there produces confusing downstream errors instead of 'parameter list shorter than number of datasets'.
findings.repro:
from hypertools.core.shared import get
print(get([1,2,3], 5), get([1,2,3], -1))
findings.expected: raise IndexError (or document + warn) when a per-dataset list is shorter than the dataset index
findings.actual:
get([1,2,3], 5) -> [1, 2, 3] (out of range returns whole list)
get([1,2,3], -1) -> [1, 2, 3] (negative index returns whole list)

findings.title: No user-facing configuration API or docs: hypertools.config is only __version__, and no documented way exists to change library-wide defaults
findings.description: The mandate question 'is config get/set documented anywhere user-facing?' — answer: no. hypertools.config exposes exactly __version__/version. get_default_options/apply_defaults exist on hypertools.core but appear in no docs page (docs/api.rst has no config entry; no tutorial mentions configuration). Users who want persistent defaults (e.g. always cmap='viridis', always ndims=2) must pass kwargs on every call. Given config.ini/configurator already exist (currently dead, see -002), 1.0 could either wire them up and document a supported set-defaults API, or delete the machinery to avoid implying configurability.
findings.repro:
import hypertools, hypertools.config as c
print([a for a in dir(c) if not a.startswith('_')])  # ['version']
# grep -rn 'get_default_options' docs/*.rst  -> no hits
findings.expected: documented hypertools-level default-setting mechanism, or removal of the inert config machinery
findings.actual:
public attrs: ['version']
docs/api.rst contains no config/exceptions entries (only prose word 'core' at line 14)
